sub_graphs.title: SSZ: Serialization and Deserialization Pipeline
sub_graphs.description: Models the encoding/decoding process for SSZ types including offset-based variable-size element handling and type-specific encoding rules

nodes.label: Typed Object in Memory
nodes.description: A well-typed SSZ value (basic type, container, list, vector, union, etc.) exists in memory ready for serialization

nodes.label: Classify Fixed vs Variable Size
nodes.description: Determine if the type is fixed-size (basic types, fixed composites) or variable-size (lists, unions, bitlists, composites with variable members)

nodes.label: Serialize Basic Type
nodes.description: Encode uintN as little-endian bytes (N/8 bytes), boolean as 0x00/0x01

nodes.label: Serialize Container
nodes.description: Concatenate fixed elements and 4-byte offsets for variable elements, then append serialized variable-size content

nodes.label: Serialize List/Bitlist
nodes.description: Serialize list elements; for bitlists append sentinel bit at position equal to length

nodes.label: Serialize Union
nodes.description: Write single selector byte (0-127) followed by serialized contained value

nodes.label: Serialized Byte String
nodes.description: Object has been deterministically serialized to a byte string

nodes.label: Deserialize with Validation
nodes.description: Reconstruct object from bytes: validate offsets, check alignment, verify list capacity, check union selector bounds

nodes.label: Deserialization Failed
nodes.description: Input bytes failed validation: malformed offsets, excess bytes, capacity violations, or invalid selector

edges.label: Receive bytes from network for deserialization
Valid bytes decoded to typed object

external_entities.name: Network Data Source
external_entities.description: Raw SSZ-encoded bytes received from P2P network, RPC responses, or other external sources

sub_graphs.title: SSZ: Merkleization and Hash Tree Roots
sub_graphs.description: Models the Merkleization process that produces hash tree roots for consensus state verification

nodes.label: Values Ready for Merkleization
nodes.description: Serialized values or field roots ready to be packed into 32-byte chunks

nodes.label: Pack Values into Chunks
nodes.description: Serialize values into 32-byte aligned chunks with zero-padding via pack() or pack_bits()

nodes.label: Compute Merkle Root
nodes.description: Build binary hash tree from chunks, zero-padding to power-of-two count, and compute root

nodes.label: Mix in Length
nodes.description: Hash root with uint256 length encoding for variable-length types (lists, bitlists)

nodes.label: Mix in Selector
nodes.description: Hash root with uint8 selector for union types

nodes.label: Mix in Active Fields
nodes.description: Hash root with active field bitmap for progressive containers

nodes.label: Progressive Merkleization
nodes.description: Recursive unbounded merkleization supporting arbitrary growth for ProgressiveList and ProgressiveContainer types

nodes.label: Hash Tree Root Computed
nodes.description: 32-byte hash tree root has been computed, usable for consensus state comparison and verification

edges.label: Progressive container needs active fields mixing
Root with active fields for progressive containers

sub_graphs.title: SSZ: Deserialization Hardening
sub_graphs.description: Models the security checks required during deserialization of untrusted SSZ data from external sources

nodes.label: Untrusted SSZ Bytes Received
nodes.description: Raw bytes received from an external untrusted source that claim to be valid SSZ

nodes.label: Validate Offset Ordering and Range
nodes.description: Check that offsets are strictly increasing, within bounds, and properly aligned to minimum element sizes

nodes.label: Check for Excess Bytes
nodes.description: Verify no trailing bytes remain after deserialization; all input bytes must be consumed

nodes.label: Validate List Capacity
nodes.description: Ensure deserialized list length does not exceed the declared maximum capacity N

nodes.label: Validate Union Selector
nodes.description: Check selector byte is in valid range (0-127) and corresponds to a defined type variant

nodes.label: Validate Bitlist Sentinel
nodes.description: Verify the sentinel bit is present and correctly positioned to determine bitlist length

nodes.label: Deserialization Safe
nodes.description: All security checks passed; data is safe for consumption by consensus logic

nodes.label: Malformed Data Rejected
nodes.description: Deserialization rejected due to failed validation; source may be malicious

external_entities.name: Untrusted Data Source
external_entities.description: Any external source of SSZ-encoded data: P2P peers, RPC clients, or stored snapshots from untrusted origins

ambiguities.text: Progressive Container and Compatible Union types support 'stable Merkleization across schema versions' but the exact forward/backward compatibility guarantees are not precisely bounded.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume progressive types guarantee that adding new fields to a container or new variants to a union does not change the hash tree root of existing data.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not detail maximum nesting depth for composite types, which could affect stack-based deserialization implementations.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations enforce a reasonable maximum nesting depth (e.g., 64 levels) to prevent stack overflow during recursive deserialization.

ambiguities.text: The term 'byte' is described as '8-bit opaque data (equivalent to uint8 in serialization)' but the semantic distinction from uint8 is unclear.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume byte and uint8 are serialization-identical; byte is used for semantic clarity when data is opaque (not arithmetic).

implicit_assumptions.description: The hash function used in Merkleization (SHA-256) is collision-resistant, ensuring distinct objects produce distinct hash tree roots.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Hash collisions could allow an attacker to substitute one state for another, breaking consensus state verification entirely.

implicit_assumptions.description: All consensus clients implement SSZ serialization identically, producing bit-identical output for the same input.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Consensus split: different clients would compute different hash tree roots for the same state, causing chain forks between client implementations.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot craft SSZ payloads that cause excessive memory allocation during deserialization within the declared size limits.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Memory exhaustion DoS: carefully crafted payloads with many small variable-length elements could amplify memory usage beyond the raw byte count.
